title: Returning traveller with fever
stem: Cubicle 5. Mr Tam, 30, has had 5 days of fever, rigors, headache and aching joints. HR 106, BP 118/70, temperature 38.9 °C, RR 18, SpO2 98%. Take a history, then discuss your differential diagnosis and investigations with the examiner.
notes:
Checked against UKHSA guidelines for malaria prevention and treatment (UK malaria treatment guidelines, 2016 with updates), WHO Guidelines for malaria (2023–2025), the CHP (Hong Kong) guidance, and the RCEM/BIA approach to the febrile returning traveller.

Malaria must be excluded in any fever within 1 year of travel to an endemic area (most falciparum within 3 months). Tests: thick and thin films (three sets over 48–72 hours if negative) plus a rapid antigen test; parasitaemia; FBC (thrombocytopenia), U&E, LFT, glucose, lactate, gas. Severe falciparum malaria: impaired consciousness or seizures, respiratory distress/acidosis, shock, AKI, hypoglycaemia, jaundice, severe anaemia, bleeding, parasitaemia 2% or more (UK threshold; WHO uses 10% in high-transmission settings): treat with IV artesunate. Uncomplicated falciparum: artemether–lumefantrine (or atovaquone–proguanil). Non-falciparum: chloroquine (or artemisinin combination), then primaquine for vivax/ovale after G6PD testing.

Your notes list quinine, doxycycline and chloroquine as the anti-malarial drugs; current first-line for severe falciparum is IV artesunate (quinine is a second-line alternative) and for uncomplicated falciparum an artemisinin combination. The rest of your history and investigation list matches.

This case: backpacking in rural Sierra Leone, no prophylaxis, thrombocytopenia and a 3% falciparum parasitaemia — severe malaria.

steps.label: Take a history
steps.hint: Fever story, systems review, detailed travel history (where, when, doing what), prophylaxis, vaccines, TOCC, PMH.

Fever.rz: 五日前開始。一陣陣咁嚟，發冷震、出汗，而家日日都係咁。
Fever.r: Started 5 days ago. Comes in waves with shaking chills and sweats, every day now.

Fever.t: Other symptoms: cough, diarrhoea, urine, rash, confusion?
Fever.tz: 仲有冇其他症狀：咳、肚屙、小便、出疹、混亂？
Fever.rz: 頭痛、關節痛，有少少想嘔。冇咳、冇出疹、冇肚屙。小便深色咗。
Fever.r: Headache, joint aches, some nausea. No cough, no rash, no diarrhoea. My urine is darker.

Travel.t: Have you travelled recently? Where exactly and when?
Travel.tz: 最近有冇去過旅行？具體去咗邊、幾時？
Travel.rz: 喺塞拉利昂背囊旅行咗三個禮拜，去鄉村。十日前返嚟。
Travel.r: Backpacking in Sierra Leone, three weeks, rural villages. Came back 10 days ago.
Travel.mark: Asks where, when and how long

Travel.t: Did you take malaria tablets? Mosquito nets?
Travel.tz: 有冇食預防瘧疾嘅藥？有冇用蚊帳？
Travel.r: I didn't take any tablets. Lots of mosquito bites.
Travel.mark: Asks about malaria prophylaxis and bite prevention

Travel.t: Fresh water swimming, animal contact, sexual contact, sick contacts?
Travel.tz: 有冇喺淡水游水、接觸動物、有性接觸，或者接觸過病人？
Travel.rz: 喺河度游過一次水。冇性接觸。我所知冇其他人病。
Travel.r: Swam in a river once. No sexual contacts. No one else ill that I know.

Travel.t: Did you visit anywhere with Ebola or Lassa outbreaks, or care for sick people?
Travel.tz: 有冇去過有伊波拉或者拉沙熱爆發嘅地方，或者照顧過病人？
Travel.rz: 冇做醫護工作，冇去喪禮，冇接觸病人。
Travel.r: No healthcare work, no funerals, no sick people.
Travel.mark: Screens for viral haemorrhagic fever risk

Background.tz: 以前有咩病？食緊咩藥？有冇敏感？
做咩工作？身邊有冇人一樣病？屋企有邊個？
Background.rz: 做寫字樓。同女朋友住，佢冇事。
Background.r: Office worker. Lives with his girlfriend, who is well.

steps.label: Examination findings and tests
steps.hint: Ask for the key signs, then films, antigen test, bloods.

Signs.t: Jaundice, pallor, rash, lymph nodes, liver and spleen
Signs.r: Mildly icteric. Spleen tip palpable. No rash.

Bloods.t: Thick and thin blood films and a malaria rapid antigen test
Bloods.mark: Requests thick and thin films and antigen test

Bloods.t: FBC, U&E, LFT, glucose, lactate, gas
Bloods.r: Platelets 54, Hb 112, creatinine 110, bilirubin 58, glucose 4.2, lactate 2.8.

Bloods.t: Blood cultures, dengue serology/NS1, HIV test
Bloods.mark: Considers other diagnoses: typhoid, dengue, HIV

steps.ask: Thank you. What is your differential diagnosis, and your plan?
steps.label: Discuss with the examiner

opts.t: Differential: falciparum malaria, dengue, typhoid, rickettsial infection, leptospirosis, HIV seroconversion; common infections too
Severe malaria: parasitaemia 2% or more (UK) with jaundice → admit, IV artesunate
opts.mark: Recognises severe malaria and treats with IV artesunate

opts.t: Infectious diseases consultant; notify the Centre for Health Protection

opts.r: West African falciparum is chloroquine-resistant, and he has severe disease.

opts.t: Wait for three negative films over 3 days before thinking of malaria
opts.r: The first film is already positive; treat now.

qs.q: First-line treatment for severe falciparum malaria?
UK parasitaemia threshold for severe malaria?
Films in suspected malaria if the first is negative?
qs.a: Repeat to three sets over 48–72 hours
wrong: Only if the patient becomes unwell on the ward
5 years of return, for most species

badge.name: Mosquito Hunter
badge.flavor: Fever after the tropics is malaria until three films say no.

cards.why: Also acidosis, shock, AKI, hypoglycaemia, anaemia, parasitaemia ≥2%.

cards.q: Which parasite relapses from liver hypnozoites?
cards.why: Needs primaquine or tafenoquine after G6PD testing.

cards.q: Thrombocytopenia with fever after Africa suggests…
options: Influenza, with nothing else to consider
Only the airline, flight number and seat
cards.why: Incubation periods and exposures guide the differential.

options: First-line for every case of severe malaria
cards.why: Artesunate reduces mortality compared with quinine.
